title: Union Parishad elections to run under old laws, leaving reform proposals aside
excerpt: The Election Commission plans UP polls in five phases from January to May 2027. Most Local Government Reform Commission ideas are not included.
content:
The Election Commission will hold Union Parishad elections in five phases between January and May 2027 under existing laws, without the changes proposed by the Electoral Reform Commission and the Local Government Reform Commission, The Daily Star reported on 9 November.

What is left out

  • Amending Article 119(1) of the Constitution so the Election Commission can hold local elections without waiting for a government request.
  • Replacing direct elections of chairmen and mayors with a parliamentary-style system in which elected councillors choose the executive head.
  • Bringing all five tiers of local government under one law and one election schedule.

The one reform the government has adopted is ending party symbols in local elections.

Who said what

“We will not go an inch beyond the existing law,” said Election Commissioner Abdur Rahmanel Masud, adding that the commission had sent proposals needing legislation but had no reply. Zahed Ur Rahman, an adviser to the prime minister, said the government would implement only the reforms in the BNP’s manifesto: “BNP does not agree with all the recommendations of the Local Government Reform Commission.”

Kazi Maruful Islam, a Dhaka University professor and former member of the Local Government Reform Commission, proposed an expert committee to review all the reform commissions’ recommendations.

Why it matters

Union Parishads are NGOs’ closest government partner, from social safety net lists to village courts and disaster committees. New chairmen and members will take office across the country in the first half of 2027, under the same rules as before. Together with the draft Gram Sarkar law, it shows the government favouring new structures over the reform commission’s changes to existing ones.

What to watch

The election schedule for the first phase, the role of non-party candidates now that party symbols are gone, and whether the Gram Sarkar law passes before the UP polls.

Sources

  • UP polls: EC sticks to old laws, key reforms left out, The Daily Star, 9 November 2026
